Angles, Radians and Degrees: Angles in standard position start on the positive x-axis, with counterclockwise turns positive. A full turn is 360 degrees or 2pi radians, so 180 degrees equals pi radians. Multiply by pi/180 to convert degrees to radians and by 180/pi for the reverse. Coterminal angles differ by full turns. For theta in radians, arc length is s = r*theta and sector area is A = (1/2) r^2 theta.
The Unit Circle: On the unit circle x^2 + y^2 = 1, the terminal side of angle theta meets the circle at (cos theta, sin theta), and tan theta = sin theta / cos theta. Hence sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1. Signs follow the quadrant: all positive in Q I, sine in Q II, tangent in Q III, cosine in Q IV. Use the reference angle to find magnitudes, then apply the quadrant sign. Coterminal angles have equal values.
Right Triangle and Reciprocal Trigonomet: In a right triangle, sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse and tan = opposite/adjacent. The reciprocals are csc = 1/sin, sec = 1/cos and cot = 1/tan. Cofunctions satisfy sin theta = cos(90 degrees - theta). The Pythagorean theorem finds a missing side. Angles of elevation and depression are measured from the horizontal, and tangent usually relates height to horizontal distance.
Graphs of Sine and Cosine: For y = A sin(B(x - C)) + D, the amplitude is the absolute value of A, the period is 2pi divided by the absolute value of B, the phase shift is C (right if positive), and the midline is y = D. The maximum is D plus the amplitude and the minimum is D minus it. A negative A reflects the graph. Five key points per cycle help sketch the wave.
Graphs of Tangent and Other Trig Functio: Tangent and cotangent have period pi; for y = A tan(Bx) the period is pi divided by the absolute value of B. Tangent has asymptotes at pi/2 + k*pi and zeros at k*pi, while cotangent has asymptotes at k*pi. Secant and cosecant have period 2pi and range y <= -1 or y >= 1 (scaled by A), with asymptotes where the related cosine or sine is zero. They never cross the x-axis.
